Title: SSH host key verification disabled by default (InsecureIgnoreHostKey)
Analysis:
In OpenTofu, when configuring an SSH connection for remote provisioning (e.g. `remote-exec`), if the user does not specify a `host_key`, the SSH communicator defaults to ignoring host key verification. 

Specifically, in `internal/communicator/ssh/provisioner.go`:
```go
func buildSSHClientConfig(opts sshClientConfigOpts) (*ssh.ClientConfig, error) {
	hkCallback := ssh.InsecureIgnoreHostKey()

	if opts.hostKey != "" {
        ...
		hkCallback, err = knownhosts.New(tf.Name())
        ...
	}

	conf := &ssh.ClientConfig{
		HostKeyCallback: hkCallback,
		User:            opts.user,
	}
```
If `opts.hostKey` is empty, `hkCallback` remains `ssh.InsecureIgnoreHostKey()`. This exposes the SSH connection to potential Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attacks, allowing an attacker to intercept or modify communication/commands sent to the remote host. OpenTofu should enforce host key verification by default or at least warn the user, rather than silently disabling it completely.

**Conceptual Exploit Payload:**
An attacker positioned on the same network or with ARP spoofing capabilities intercepts the SSH connection from the machine running OpenTofu to the target server during the apply phase. Since OpenTofu uses `ssh.InsecureIgnoreHostKey()`, it will authenticate against the attacker's server without warning, allowing the attacker to capture SSH credentials or execute arbitrary code on the runner/provisioner by redirecting the session.
